dropped.8: JournalStore gained a required readStep(runId, key) method, so a host that IMPLEMENTS the interface no longer satisfies it — the whole point of RuntimeOptions.journal being that a deployment with its own database supplies one. The frozen templates only CONSUME a journal, so they still compile; that is the documented gap between classification coverage and compile-time exercise, not evidence the epoch holds. Consumers add the method: it answers ONE settled step by key, undefined when it has not settled, and both shipped databases key the table (run_id, key) so it is an index seek.
dropped.9: JournalStore gained a required readSleeps(runId) method, so a host that IMPLEMENTS the interface no longer satisfies it — the whole point of RuntimeOptions.journal being that a deployment with its own database supplies one. The frozen templates only CONSUME a journal, so they still compile; that is the documented gap between classification coverage and compile-time exercise, not evidence the epoch holds. Consumers add the method: it answers EVERY durable wait of a run, ordered by key, as SleepEntry (a SleepRecord plus its key), and both shipped databases key the sleeps table (run_id, key) so it is a range scan already in that order. It is what stops a replay re-claiming every elapsed sleep it walks past — measured in production at 2,675 journal POSTs on one run, rising +1 per delivery across 69 deliveries.
